messages.author: 96d32d9538ca9afa
messages.subject: Error: Failed to create the shared library
parts:
Hi,

I am new to Nimble, and have seen several other threads with similar issues as my own. I have a 64 bit Windows 10 machine and have tried reinstalling Rtools, and the newest version of R 4.0.0 to no avail. Keep on getting the error "Failed to create the shared library". Completely at a loss after hours of messing with this.

Please help.

Thanks,
Chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library
parts:
Hi Chris,

Can you use "showCompilerOutput = TRUE" as an argument to nimbleModel and share the output please.  An alternative is, in a separate call, to do "nimbleOptions(showCompilerOutput = TRUE)".

Also please show the code you are using.  I assume it is one of our examples but want to be sure.

You said you've seen several other relevant threads.  I want to draw attention to the Rtools FAQ here : https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/.  

Can you try reinstalling in the following order: R, Rtools, nimble.  

-Perry

Hi Perry,

Thanks for your help. The code is a simple linear regression from a course at North Carolina State U (https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~reich/BSMdata/software.html). I will try reinstalling in the order you suggest in the meantime.


set.seed(0820)

nimbleOptions(showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
model_string <- nimbleCode({
  for(i in 1:n){
    mass[i] ~ dnorm(mn[i],tau)
    mn[i]  <- beta1 + beta2*age[i]
  }
  tau   ~  dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
  beta1 ~  dnorm(0, 0.0000001)
  beta2 ~  dnorm(0, 0.0000001)
})

consts   <- list(n=n,age=age)
data     <- list(mass=mass)
inits    <- function(){list(beta1=rnorm(1),beta2=rnorm(1),tau=10)}
samples  <- nimbleMCMC(model_string, data = data, inits = inits,
                       constants=consts,
                       monitors = c("beta1", "beta2"),
                       samplesAsCodaMCMC=TRUE,WAIC=FALSE,
                       niter = 30000, nburnin = 10000, nchains = 2)

messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library
parts:
There are three cpp files (each with a .cpp and .h) compiled for a model and MCMC, two for the model, one for the MCMC.  It looks like the C++ compiler is found but there are errors that look like linking errors.

I think the failure to find the final dll that you copied is the last downstream manifestation of earlier compilation errors, which look like linking errors.

These are, unfortunately, difficult problems for us to diagnose in that they seem to be system-specific, unless there is some change associated with Rtools40 that we need to learn about. 

Can I suggest a few experiments (each separate):

Try installing nimble from source: install.packages("nimble", type = "source")

Be sure your R session has administrative privileges.

Try using "dirName = 'some_local_dir'" in your calls to compileNimble.  (You will have to switch from using nimbleMCMC to building and compiling the model and MCMC directly, with nimbleModel -> buildMCMC -> compileNimble.  However the problem might manifest just from compiling the model, without an MCMC involved.)

Try installing nimble in a local directory (lib argument to install.packages, then lib.loc argument to library).

-Perry

On Wednesday, April 29, 2020 at 6:17:16 PM UTC-5, pdevalpine wrote:

There are three cpp files (each with a .cpp and .h) compiled for a model and MCMC, two for the model, one for the MCMC.  It looks like the C++ compiler is found but there are errors that look like linking errors.

I think the failure to find the final dll that you copied is the last downstream manifestation of earlier compilation errors, which look like linking errors.

These are, unfortunately, difficult problems for us to diagnose in that they seem to be system-specific, unless there is some change associated with Rtools40 that we need to learn about. 

Can I suggest a few experiments (each separate):

Try installing nimble from source: install.packages("nimble", type = "source")

Be sure your R session has administrative privileges.

Try using "dirName = 'some_local_dir'" in your calls to compileNimble.  (You will have to switch from using nimbleMCMC to building and compiling the model and MCMC directly, with nimbleModel -> buildMCMC -> compileNimble.  However the problem might manifest just from compiling the model, without an MCMC involved.)

Try installing nimble in a local directory (lib argument to install.packages, then lib.loc argument to library).

-Perry

messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library
parts:
Hi Chris and Perry,

I applied the fix you suggested to another user who posted the issue "Nimble unable to find dll after upgrade to R4 / rtools40" and it worked. Thank you for the help and providing a solution.

All the best,
Chris

On Thursday, April 30, 2020 at 9:24:59 AM UTC-5, Christopher Jennelle wrote:
Thabnk you Perry - I will try your suggestions. After trying the first one, installing Nimble from 'source', I get the following error/warning:

> install.packages("nimble", type = "source")
Error in install.packages : Updating loaded packages

Restarting R session...

Loading required package: nimble
Error in .requirePackage(package) : 
  unable to find required package ‘nimble’
In addition: Warning message:
In library(package, lib.loc = lib.loc, character.only = TRUE, logical.return = TRUE,  :
  there is no package called ‘nimble’

On Wednesday, April 29, 2020 at 6:17:16 PM UTC-5, pdevalpine wrote:
There are three cpp files (each with a .cpp and .h) compiled for a model and MCMC, two for the model, one for the MCMC.  It looks like the C++ compiler is found but there are errors that look like linking errors.

I think the failure to find the final dll that you copied is the last downstream manifestation of earlier compilation errors, which look like linking errors.

These are, unfortunately, difficult problems for us to diagnose in that they seem to be system-specific, unless there is some change associated with Rtools40 that we need to learn about. 

Can I suggest a few experiments (each separate):

Try installing nimble from source: install.packages("nimble", type = "source")

Be sure your R session has administrative privileges.

Try using "dirName = 'some_local_dir'" in your calls to compileNimble.  (You will have to switch from using nimbleMCMC to building and compiling the model and MCMC directly, with nimbleModel -> buildMCMC -> compileNimble.  However the problem might manifest just from compiling the model, without an MCMC involved.)

Try installing nimble in a local directory (lib argument to install.packages, then lib.loc argument to library).

-Perry
